ownership.quote: Founded in 2020, UK-owned and EU-Sovereign, we’re the full-stack AI cloud platform, providing sustainable AI solutions at scale.

stage.quote: LONDON, April 08, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NexGen Cloud, a UK leader in AI infrastructure, has closed its Series A round, raising $45 million at a $354 million valuation.
stage.note: Last priced equity round is this April 2025 Series A. A June 2026 $34M facility from USD.AI is described as a non-recourse debt financing to fund GPU hardware, not an equity round, so it does not change the stage.

total_funding_usd.basis: Compworth aggregator: 'NexGen Cloud has completed 3 funding rounds, raising $64.4M in total.' No primary source states a cumulative equity total; the confirmed Series A alone is $45M.
total_funding_usd.quote: NexGen Cloud has completed 3 funding rounds, raising $64.4M in total.

last_round.quote: NexGen Cloud, a UK leader in AI infrastructure, has closed its Series A round, raising $45 million at a $354 million valuation. Backed by high-net-worth individuals and family trusts, the funding will drive global expansion and strengthen sovereign AI capabilities in Europe.

revenue.basis: £72 million converted at ~1.27 USD/GBP (approximate); figure is the company's own stated revenue for FY2023-2024.
revenue.quote: Since launching Hyperstack in 2023, NexGen Cloud has generated £72 million in revenue (2023-2024), driven by a 380% rise in AI cloud revenue and a 2,272% surge in transactions.

note: Hyperstack is the GPU-cloud brand of NexGen Cloud, a UK (London-based) company founded 2020, still independent/privately held (no acquisition or parent found). No accelerator/incubator affiliation found. In addition to the $45M Series A (Apr 2025), NexGen Cloud also announced a separate $34M non-recourse debt facility from USD.AI (June 2026) to finance GPU hardware deployment in Sweden — debt, not equity, so excluded from funding stage/round figures above but worth noting to a buyer as another capital source. No accelerator batch, no public IPO; total funding figure is a third-party estimate (Compworth) not corroborated by a primary source.
